newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Outer space drugs for earthling diseases.
newsitem.headline: Outer space drugs for earthling diseases.

text.p: Drugs to combat insect-borne illnesses that infect a quarter of a million people each year in Latin America may soon be developed in outer space, the United Nations said on Monday.
The UN Outer Space Scientific and Technical Subcommittee said it would launch an experiment next month whereby parasitic enzymes would be crystallised in micro-gravity aboard spacecraft.
The large, well-formed crystals are required for the production of therapeutic agents necessary to fight diseases such as chagas, spread by the vinchuga fly.
The insect bites sleeping people, usually children, in the eye region, secreting parasites that can be passed on via blood transfusions or the placenta.

Problems in the production of such crystals on earth have been the main obstacle to fighting chagas. The crystallisation process also offers hope for more effective treatment of other human diseases, including diabetes.
